trigger.reason: A new studio course needs a coherent progression from looking carefully to producing and explaining a measured drawing.
inspectedEvidence: Instructor notes from three introductory drawing cohorts
Representative first-session and final-session learner drawings
Studio brief for the proposed course

programme.subject: Observational drawing through proportion, negative space, and revision
programme.scope: A six-session studio course in which beginners learn to observe, measure, revise, and explain one drawing from life
programme.audience: Adults beginning observational drawing without prior studio training
programme.startingPoint: Learners can name the objects they see but often draw remembered symbols instead of comparing visible relationships

thesis.recognisedProblem: A beginner may look continuously at a subject while still drawing the idea of the object rather than its visible proportions and spaces.
thesis.promisedLearnerChange: Learners leave able to construct, test, revise, and explain an observational drawing using visible proportional and spatial relationships.
thesis.centralQuestion: How can a learner draw what is visibly present instead of the convenient symbol already held in memory?
thesis.distinctiveArgument: Observation becomes a learnable craft when learners externalise comparison, test relationships on the page, and preserve revision as evidence of seeing more accurately.
thesis.argumentBoundary: The course develops introductory observational practice and does not prescribe one expressive style or assess professional artistic merit.
thesis.changedCondition: The proposed course replaces demonstration-heavy classes with repeated short cycles of observation, comparison, drawing, and revision.

transformationLens.reason: The course is a greenfield craft progression and does not depend on an inherited operating form or technological transformation claim.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: Beginning learners in the instructor's prior cohorts often substituted familiar object symbols for observed proportional relationships.
evidenceBoundaries.attribution: Course instructor's comparison of learner work and critique notes
evidenceBoundaries.observedScope: Three introductory adult cohorts taught by the instructor, with twelve representative drawing sequences reviewed
evidenceBoundaries.known: The reviewed sequences contain repeated mismatches between stated observation and relationships drawn on the page.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The small teaching sample does not establish how common the pattern is across drawing education.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use to frame this course's learner problem within the observed cohorts and proposed studio design.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: The commissioned course prioritises repeated learner practice and revision over long instructor demonstrations.
evidenceBoundaries.observedScope: The design requirements recorded for this six-session introductory course
evidenceBoundaries.known: The brief specifies short demonstrations followed by observable learner practice in every session.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The optimum duration of each practice cycle will require adjustment after the first cohort.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use to determine the course architecture while preserving timing as a pilot variable.

evidenceBoundaries.claim: Externalised comparison and visible revision can organise a progression from looking to measured observational drawing.
evidenceBoundaries.known: The learner problem and commissioned practice format both make comparison and revision observable on the page.
evidenceBoundaries.uncertain: The progression still needs learner testing before it can be treated as a generally effective sequence.
evidenceBoundaries.allowedUse: Use as the bounded design proposition for this course and revise it from portfolio evidence.

carriedProof.name: Seeing and Revision Portfolio
carriedProof.initialState: An unmeasured first drawing accompanied by the learner's account of what was noticed
carriedProof.finalState: A drawing revised through explicit proportion and negative-space checks with the changes explained
carriedProof.successEvidence: The learner can identify a visible relationship, show how it was tested, revise the drawing, and explain what changed in the observation.

capabilityProgression.learnerMove: Learners compare the height, width, angle, and placement of major shapes before outlining named objects.
capabilityProgression.proofAdded: The portfolio marks at least three measured relationships used to place the main shapes.
capabilityProgression.handoff: Placed shapes create enclosed spaces whose accuracy can be tested without relying on object names.

capabilityProgression.learnerMove: Learners compare the shapes around and between objects to detect errors in placement and proportion.
capabilityProgression.proofAdded: The portfolio shows one negative-space comparison and the correction it caused.
capabilityProgression.handoff: The corrected construction can now be developed and revised without concealing the evidence of change.

capabilityProgression.learnerMove: Learners test the developed drawing against the subject, revise a consequential relationship, and explain the evidence for that revision.
capabilityProgression.proofAdded: The final portfolio preserves the before state, the observed discrepancy, the revision, and the learner's explanation.
capabilityProgression.handoff: The learner can apply the same observation and revision cycle to a new subject without an instructor demonstration.

antiGoals: polished final images with no visible revision evidence

approval.provenance: The course owner approved the craft progression, evidence boundary, and portfolio proof in the design review.

productionDecision.nextAction: Build the six studio sessions backward from the Seeing and Revision Portfolio.
